title: Conclusion
body: Conclusion Integrating Microsoft Fabric with GitHub converts analytics development from a set of direct changes to live workspaces into a governed engineering practice. The mechanics are not difficult. What makes the difference between an implementation that holds and one that quietly degrades is a small number of decisions made deliberately at the start. Three of those decisions carry most of the weight. The first is treating the initial connection as an irreversible, change-controlled event, because it is the one step that can destroy work with no route back. The second is externalizing every environment-specific value before enabling isolated development, because without it the isolation is nominal and the confidence it creates is misplaced. The third is enforcing the controls in the repository rather than describing them in a document, because a control that depends on people remembering is a preference. The rest — the branching model, the team structure, the ruleset configuration, the credential scoping — is well-trodden and largely mechanical. It is set out here in detail so that it can be implemented consistently rather than reinvented per project, and so that the reasoning behind each choice is available to whoever has to revisit it. What the framework delivers is narrow and worth stating precisely: every change to production content is versioned, reviewed by someone other than its author, attributable, and reversible. Not that changes will be correct — no process delivers that — but that an incorrect change is caught before it ships more often than not, and can be undone when it is not. Before issuing this document Resolve every placeholder. Record the decisions in Appendix G. Delete the LOCALIZE callouts and the Status line on the cover page. Re-verify the supported-item inventory in Section 9 and the preview caveats throughout against current vendor documentation, and note the verification date in the revision history.

body: Fine-grained PAT permission reference Token configuration Token name fabric-<proj>-sync Identifies purpose. Include the project so a person holding several tokens can tell them apart. Expiration The shortest interval the team can operate with Anything beyond 90 days should require a stated justification. Resource owner The organization that owns the repository May require approval by an organization owner before the token becomes usable. Repository access Only select repositories → this project's repository Never All repositories. Repository permissions → Contents Read and write The minimum required for Fabric to read from and write to the repository. Repository permissions → Metadata Read Granted implicitly and required. label: Appendix H
title: Troubleshooting
body: Troubleshooting Common symptoms and causes The Git integration tab does nothing. A tenant switch is disabled — most often the GitHub-specific one, which is separate from the general Git integration switch. Confirm all switches in Section 4.2, including Users can sync workspace items with GitHub repositories. A developer sees no Git information at all in the workspace. They hold the Viewer workspace role. A Viewer sees no Git information regardless of repository permission. Grant Contributor or above on the workspace (Section 15.5). Commit is greyed out or fails. Updates are pending, or the connected branch is protected against direct commits. Update first. If the workspace is connected to main, it is an update target — commit from a branch workspace instead (Section 16.3). Commit fails on a protected branch. The ruleset requires a pull request. Expected. Use a branch workspace on a feature branch. Update is greyed out. A conflict exists on at least one item. Resolve the conflict (Section 8.7). Workspace items disappeared after connecting. Update workspace from Git was chosen against an empty or near-empty folder. Section 7.5. This is what the preflight clone exists for. Newly created folders vanished. Update from Git was run with an uncommitted structural change outstanding. Section 7.4. Commit structural changes before updating. Branch-out fails. No available capacity; workspace creation not permitted; the branch workspace admin profile is invalid; a naming limit exceeded. Check capacity first, then the profile's validity (Section 12.5), then names against Section 6.4. Branch-out succeeds but the workspace is empty of data. Working as designed — data is not copied. Section 13. A notebook in a branch workspace writes to shared data. No parameterization. The item still references the source workspace's lakehouse. Section 13.3. This is a design gap, not a bug. An item shows Unsupported. The item type is not covered by the integration. Section 10.3. The item is ignored, not deleted. A file fails to sync. File size above 25 MB, or full path above 250 characters. Section 6.4, and enforce the rules in Section 16.5 so this surfaces at push. A large diff appears with no functional change. Line-ending conversion, or column reordering in a .bim after a rename. Section 8.6. Expected; not a review finding. Duplicate items appear after a restore. An item was restored from the recycle bin and also re-created by a Git operation, producing two different item IDs. Delete the item Git re-created (Section 7.5). A workflow cannot read a secret. The secret is environment-scoped and the job does not target that environment, or the branch is not permitted to deploy to it. Section 17.2. Automation authentication fails. The tenant setting Service principals can call Fabric public APIs is off; the principal is not in the allow-list; it lacks a workspace role; or the client secret has expired. Section 5.4, then Section 17.4. A connection prompt appears in a workspace already connected to Git. Expected — the Git connection is per user. Configure your own connection under Account details (Section 5.3). Branch-out no longer works after it previously did. The branch workspace admin profile has become invalid — a revoked permission, a deactivated capacity, or the consented admin has left the tenant. Section 12.5. A workspace admin must resolve the issue and re-save the profile.
